servers.server_cost: No separate price; only for existing Shapes customers ("Existing Shapes customers can connect directly"), others contact sales
servers.linked_cost: Core $8 per seat/month, Plus $12 per seat/month (billed annually), minimum subscription (size not given); Surveys, Performance and Compensation modules priced on request
servers.pricing: Per-seat SaaS subscription; MCP not mentioned in the plan feature lists
servers.restrictions: OAuth sign-in with each employee's own Shapes account; "Your existing Shapes permissions carry through to every Claude conversation"; the Claude connector is set up by the organisation's administrator. Rate limits not documented.
servers.governance_logic: According to the documentation (not verifiable): 1) Read-only at the level of the whole server - no writing tools at all. 2) User permissions carry over ("you can only access data you're authorized to see"), filtering on the Shapes side. 3) Aggregating tools compute statistics instead of returning raw records. 4) Separate "my" tools for the user's own data. Human confirmation, confidence scores, logging not described.
servers.structure_note: Flat set of tools (according to the documentation)
servers.actions_comment: 35 according to mcp.shapes.co ("35+ tools"), all read-only
servers.agent_cannot: Any changes: create or change an employee, book time off, answer a survey, carry out a review, upload or sign a document (Docs & eSign). Compensation: promised "compensation gaps" analysis but no salary tool in the list (possibly via employee fields - unconfirmed). Shapes AI functions (Vibe Views, Shapes Agents, Workflows).
servers.docs_recs: None explicit; no recommendations on human confirmation (not needed, read-only) or on handling personal data in an AI chat.
servers.gov_promises: "Shapes is SOC2 certified and GDPR compliant so your people data stays protected, always"; "Your permissions carry over" / "No one sees more than they should". Privacy policy: AI features may use unnamed third-party LLM providers; data stored in Israel, EEA, UK, USA etc.; Shapes may train models on product usage data after removing personal data; customer data governed by a DPA and the "AI Modules Schedule". HR data received by the AI client goes to the AI provider - not mentioned in the MCP documentation.
servers.user_promises: "Connect in minutes. No engineering required."; the AI can answer about "attrition risk, headcount, and compensation gaps"
servers.promises_vs_logic: Read-only confirmed by the tool names (only list_, get_, aggregate_, search_, read_). Compensation analysis not confirmed by the tool list.

observations.text: The "safest" design: read-only server with permissions inherited from the user. The risks shift to confidentiality rather than actions: the AI sees sensitive HR data (examples mention "gender breakdown", birthdays, time-off balances).
Aggregating tools: the server computes statistics itself instead of giving the AI raw records.
Third-party wrappers (Knit) with write rights exist in parallel with the official server; the research must distinguish the official server from intermediaries.
Closed code + OAuth: without a customer account a researcher cannot obtain even the tool descriptions.
